chunks: He makes the night enter the day and makes the day enter the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon; each runs [its course] for a specified term. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion. And those whom you invoke other than Him do not possess [so much as] the membrane of a date seed.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the power of false gods compared to Allah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores Tawhid al-Rububiyyah by illustrating Allah's seamless control over cosmic cycles, where the 'insertion' of night into day signifies His continuous creative act. The mention of the sun and moon running for a 'specified term' (ajal musamma) highlights the precision of divine decree, while the metaphor of the 'bit of a date pit' (qitmir) vividly contrasts the omnipotent Creator with the utter impotence of idols, a theme frequently cited by scholars like Allamah Tabatabai to refute polytheism.
